title: Cuba Austin and how Jones came to the high sock cymbal
summary: He explains that he raised the sock cymbal on a pipe and a coat hanger out of necessity after seeing Cuba Austin's low model.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: ...What can you say about Cuba and who was he with?

He was with McKinney Cotton Pickers; and I saw him and he had this little sock cymbal that you used to slide your foot in. I have one at the shop. And by me running around like I said, all my friends never had what I had, the carnivals and circuses and what have you. It was through necessity that I went and got a pipe. I couldn't go down there and play that sock cymbal down there on the floor. So I had a great big stand-up drum and I had a cymbal holder that was a coathanger and put that on there. That's how the sock cymbal came, you know, like Bob Burns and his bazooka.

Yes, unfortunately, yes. But the man that - Hamilton, he was playing with Paul Whiteman's band, so they'd say, 'Hi-boy.' Before then it was down on the floor and Cuba Austin had this little thing where you used to slide your foot in. It had a little overlapping thing and then they made a little short one. I have one and then he'd go down and.... at the shop... But then they didn't have it up here. As recent as 1934 when I told you I stood down and saw you with Erskine Tate when I came from the World's Fair, nobody had a sock cymbal but Alvin Burroughs. George Wettling, Gene Krupa - they didn't know nothing about a sock cymbal. They had a sock cymbal but they put it in the closet or left it in the home. Tubby, Zitty, those guys, they never played the sock cymbal, but mine was through necessity, because that's all I had.
